rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at mid temperature to reveal the full elution window and reduce risk of missing late compounds. This should show whether peaks are unretained, retained into the hold, or spread across the gradient so later runs can tighten the window and adjust slope.

Only one pair is limiting and all peaks elute within 10 min, so the next question is whether that pair responds to gradient slope. Doubling tG while keeping the same window and temperature makes the gradient much shallower and should reveal if the critical pair can be spread apart by slope control.

The critical pair is strongly slope-sensitive: at 20 min it co-elutes, at 40 min all pairs are resolved, so the optimum should lie between them. A modest increase to 24 min tests whether full resolution can be achieved while keeping the last peak close to 10 min and preserving a high CRF.

The crossover to full resolution appears to be well above 24 min, so test 32 min to bracket the minimum tG that resolves the 4/5 pair. This should indicate whether we can then fine-tune near the threshold for the best balance of full resolution and run time.

Changing slope created a new severe coelution, so temperature is the better orthogonal lever to probe next. A lower temperature may shift selectivity enough to separate the critical close pairs while keeping the favorable short run near the 20 min gradient.

At 25 C the method is nearly ideal, with only one pair slightly below 1.5 and only a small time penalty. A small increase in tG should gently improve that marginal pair enough to reach full resolution without pushing t_last much further past 10 min.

Probe temperature one grid step above 25 C while keeping the favorable 20 min gradient to map the selectivity optimum around the nearly ideal condition. This will show whether the critical pair improves or worsens with temperature and guide whether to refine by temperature or by changing the gradient window instead.

At 25 C the only remaining issue is a slightly under-resolved mid-run pair, so trim the gradient window to the actual elution region to make the slope shallower where the peaks are without increasing tG. This should improve selectivity/resolution for the clustered middle peaks while avoiding unnecessary time spent from 0.05 to 0.95 organic.

The narrowed window at 25 C gives full resolution but with too much time penalty, so now shorten the gradient to recover CRF while staying in the better-shaped window. This tests whether full resolution can be retained with a slightly faster method closer to the 10 min target.

We now have full resolution with only a small time penalty, so the next step is to shorten the method until a pair falls below 1.5. Testing 16 min should show whether we can move t_last closer to 10 min and improve on the current best CRF.

At 16 min the method is very close to ideal, with only one pair slightly below full-credit resolution and no time penalty, so a temperature tweak is the best orthogonal refinement. Testing 30 C checks whether that marginal pair can be pushed above 1.5 without lengthening the run.

The weak pair at short gradients clearly shifts with temperature, and the order of the most critical pair may be changing around this region. Testing a higher temperature at the same fast method maps that selectivity trend and checks whether a different close pair becomes favorable enough to beat the current best.

The current best is already near-optimal, and shortening from 18 to 16 min improved CRF despite a slight loss in one pair's resolution. A 14 min gradient at the same favorable 25 C tests whether the time gain can outweigh any further small resolution loss and potentially push CRF even closer to 1.

The limiting pair at 16 min and 25 C is an early-mid pair, so raising phi0 should compress the earliest part of the run and devote more of the gradient to that cluster while keeping the successful upper end. This may improve the marginal 3/4 resolution without introducing a time penalty.

Raising phi0 from 0.10 to 0.15 improved CRF slightly and kept the same marginal pair as the only limiter, so continue in that direction. Another step higher may further focus the gradient on the crowded region and nudge that pair closer to full credit while still keeping all peaks within 10 min.

Since 14 min was too fast and 16 min gave a perfect score, test one step longer to see whether full resolution is maintained with extra margin and how sensitive the optimum is. This helps confirm that injection 16 is truly at or near the shortest fully resolved method.
